newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul mulls oil loan to refiners from govt stocks.
newsitem.headline: Seoul mulls oil loan to refiners from govt stocks.

text.p: The South Korean government is considering lending oil to local refiners to reduce petroleum imports at a time of high oil prices, a senior government official said on Wednesday.

"We are considering releasing oil from the government's stockpile as a possible measure to soften the impact of high oil prices on our economy," Byun Jong-rip, director of petroleum policy division at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, told Reuters.
But he declined to give the amount of the possible loan under consideration.
"We'll take into consideration the nation's demand and supply situation and availability of our stockpile before deciding on any action," Byun said.
The government's stockpile, which is controlled by the state-owned Korea Petroleum Development Corp, currently holds 42.6 million barrels of oil. More than 90 percent of the stock is crude oil.
Refiners are normally required to repay government oil loans in three months.
Industry sources said rising crude prices on the international market have been pressuring South Korea's current account deficit and spurring inflation.
South Korea produces no crude oil of its own, relying entirely on imports.
Its current account deficit widened to $15.2 billion for the first eight months of this year, compared with $7.3 billion a year earlier.
The consumer price index rose 4.7 percent for the first nine months of this year, exceeding the government's full-year target of 4.5 percent.
